title: Dad's Place Still Says My Last WORDS 🔊
premise: In a town where the last thing said in a house keeps playing out loud until somebody says something new, I've spent two years sure my dad's place over his auto shop was yelling my "don't call me again" at him, while a pickup parks outside my building every night with somebody in it.
twist: The voice in Dad's place is his own, "I'm going to go get him": he walked out after me that night and never went back in, and the truck outside my building is him, every night, trying to knock. I call him home in my own words and we say sorry at the same time.
world: A street of painted clapboard houses, an apartment block and its lot under one sodium streetlight, and a red-brick auto shop with an outside stair up to one room and a kitchen nook.
